title: Closures: Adder, Counter, Appender
hints:
`make_adder`: capture `n` by value and return the lambda directly; the conversion to `std::function<int(int)>` is automatic.
```cpp
return [n](int x) { return x + n; };
```

`make_counter` needs state that lives inside the closure and changes on every call: an init-capture plus `mutable`. Without `mutable` the compiler refuses to modify a by-value capture.
```cpp
return [count = 0]() mutable { return ++count; };
```

`make_appender`: the vector belongs to the caller and outlives the closure, so capture it by reference; capture `value` by copy. `[=]` would copy the whole vector into the closure: `push_back` on that copy then fails to compile (by-value captures are `const` unless the lambda is `mutable`), and with `mutable` it compiles and silently fills the private copy, leaving the caller's `sink` empty.
```cpp
return [&sink, value]() { sink.push_back(value); };
```
